questions.question: What is enjambment and what effect can it create?
questions.correctAnswer: Enjambment is when a sentence runs over the end of a line without punctuation. Effects: creates forward momentum, links ideas, reflects continuous action or thought, sounds natural and conversational.

questions.question: What's the difference between a caesura and an end-stopped line?
questions.correctAnswer: Caesura is a pause WITHIN a line (usually with punctuation). End-stopped lines have punctuation AT the end. Caesura slows within the line; end-stopped lines complete the thought before the next.

questions.question: What are the features of a Shakespearean sonnet?
questions.correctAnswer: Shakespearean sonnet: 14 lines, iambic pentameter, ABAB CDCD EFEF GG rhyme scheme. Three quatrains present problem; final couplet provides resolution or twist.
